sara_sales: New POC kickoff with AcmeCorp tomorrow. They want Redwood Private deployed into their VPC via an on-prem proxy + PrivateLink for egress preservation. Key asks: preserve client src IP, support split-tunnel (only to Redwood domains), and pass their security questionnaire. Also they asked about pricing for connector bandwidth. Can infra + security help with a preflight checklist?

aj_engineer: +1. Quick checklist off the top: 1) Decide PrivateLink vs VPC peering. PrivateLink gives isolation (interface endpoints) and is usually easier for cross-account controlled access. Peering shares routes. 2) If they need source IP preserved to their backend, we need to run TCP proxy in their network or use NAT with preserved source (BYOIP/EIP mapping). 3) Firewall rules: allow outbound tcp/443 to our endpoint ENI range and return traffic. 4) Healthcheck ports: 443 and 10254 for agent (if using on-prem agent).

mike_netops: For split-tunnel: they should route only `*.redwood-inference.com` (or our PrivateLink endpoint IPs) over the tunnel. Anything else stays local. We provide a small CIDR list for endpoint ENIs. Eg `10.55.198.0/26` (example) — we'll give concrete list in the handoff.

liz_security: Security checklist: TLS mTLS optional for customer-facing connectors. Ask for: network flow logs, endpoint SGs locked to customer subnet(s), KMS integration for keys, and audit log retention requirement. They'll also need an approved IP allowlist for any egress proxy we ask them to open.

sara_sales: They specifically asked: "If we use PrivateLink, do we need to open outbound internet to reach updates/telemetry?" Also pricing: is connector bandwidth billed separately or included in Private plan?

aj_engineer: PrivateLink itself doesn't require general internet egress for inference traffic — it's direct. But telemetry/updates may need outbound to our control plane (unless on air-gapped plan). For Private (VPC) deployments we can optionally funnel control-plane telemetry over the PrivateLink endpoint; otherwise, minimal outbound to `control.redwood-inference.com` over 443.

mike_netops: On billing: connector/bandwidth depends on contract. Standard Dedicated includes baseline reserved capacity; egress/egress-proxy data transfer often shows up in cloud bandwidth costs too. For POC we can offer a capped trial bandwidth rate — I can confirm numbers with sales ops.

liz_security: For their security questionnaire: include ACL snippets and sample SG: ```Inbound: Type HTTPS, Protocol TCP, Port 443, Source sg-12345 (customer-proxy) Outbound: All traffic to sg-redwood-endpoint (443)``` Also include example firewall NAT rule to preserve src: `NETMAP 10.0.0.0/24 -> 198.51.100.0/24` (vendor-specific).

aj_engineer: Practical test steps for POC: 1) Customer creates PrivateLink interface endpoint in their account and attaches SG that allows tcp/443 from their proxy. 2) They spin up the on-prem proxy with static NAT and run `curl -v https://<endpoint-ip>/healthz` from behind the proxy to validate TLS handshake. 3) We provide a test API key for low-rate calls to validate inference path. Example curl: ``curl -H "Authorization: Bearer test-poc-key" https://endpoint-10-55-198-12.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'``

mike_netops: Ports checklist: tcp/443 outbound from customer proxy to PrivateLink endpoint. If using management agent: tcp/22 for initial debug (optional, gated), tcp/443 for agent heartbeat. If they insist on deep packet inspection (TLS terminate), we need either mTLS or a proxy that preserves SNI.

sara_sales: They also raised an enterprise blocker: their legal team wants a statement on egress IP stability (for their firewall allowlist). They want to know if endpoint IPs change often.

aj_engineer: We provide stable ENI IP ranges per region for the lifetime of the customer's deployment. During major infra changes IPs might change but we'd do coordinated change windows and provide new lists 30 days prior. Add this to the SLA/handshake doc.

liz_security: Addendum: if they require static public egress IPs (for on-prem to internet), customer needs to NAT via a stable EIP. For PrivateLink, source IP preservation is handled by their proxy; Redwood won't rewrite client IP. Document that clearly in the security questionnaire answers.

sara_sales: Great. Can someone produce a short handoff doc for the SEs: required SG rules, sample NAT snippet, test curl, and the list of docs to attach to the questionnaire? I can send to the customer by EOD. :pray: 

aj_engineer: I'll draft the handoff. Will include: - Minimal SG/ACL snippets - Example curl & sample payloads - Billing note (POC capped bandwidth) - Preflight checklist (interface endpoint, proxy NAT, DNS entry) - Escalation contacts for on-call.

deploy-bot: Deployment checklist ticket created: #POC-4821. Assigning to aj_engineer and mike_netops. :white_check_mark: 

mike_netops: I'll follow up with the exact ENI CIDR list (region-based) and confirm the POC bandwidth cap number with finance later today.

sara_sales: Awesome. Sending draft email to customer after your handoff doc. Thanks team! :tada:
